category_title: Students with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) showing variable engagement
student_description: This student with ASD struggles to engage during whole-class instruction, often becoming inattentive or misbehaving without direct support. While they respond well academically to 1:1 teaching, this heavy individual support tends to isolate them socially, causing them to ignore peers. They uniquely require a delicate balance of direct, individualized academic prompting and actively scaffolded peer interactions to achieve both academic access and true social inclusion.

criteria.rationale: Over-reliance on 1:1 support isolates this student, so their long-term plan must deliberately balance individual academic help with cooperative peer activities.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term plan explicitly includes both dedicated 1:1 instructional time and structured cooperative learning activities with peers.

criteria.rationale: The student benefits from true inclusion, which is undermined if the general education teacher pulls back and leaves all instruction to the special education teacher.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term strategy explicitly requires both the general education teacher and the special education teacher to actively instruct and interact with the student.
